recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is for FHIR-26660. Do not change the PackagedProductDefinition.name search parameter under this issue; handle that separately only if FHIR-57440 or another final BR&R decision is applied.
issue_request: FHIR-26660 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request for R5 asking to add PackagedProductDefinition.name as a 0..1 string so package-specific names do not have to be carried in the textual description element.
initial_application: No current-branch commit message explicitly mentions FHIR-26660. The current ancestry first introduced the active PackagedProductDefinition StructureDefinition in commit 33b409a4b6, and that file already contained PackagedProductDefinition.name with min 0, max 1, and type string, followed by a separate description element.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has PackagedProductDefinition as an active resource and maps the legacy MedicinalProductPackaged artifact name to PackagedProductDefinition, so this is the current build-scope source for the Jira related artifact. The R5 published profile also exposes PackagedProductDefinition.name as 0..1 string. BR&R's 2020-03-31 minutes list FHIR-26660 among the PQ/CMC-to-IDMP trackers with decisions recorded on Jira. A later Zulip thread about an ePI IG constraint confirms that core/R5 kept the package name optional and discusses why packages may not always have names. FHIR-57440 now raises the separate concern that the PackagedProductDefinition.name search parameter is token despite the string element, but that issue is Submitted/unresolved and is not a final decision for this reconciliation.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The published empty audit commit records that the active current source already satisfies the approved request by defining PackagedProductDefinition.name as 0..1 string and keeping PackagedProductDefinition.description as separate descriptive markdown.
